source.edition: Translated and annotated by Justin O'Brien, Alfred A. Knopf, 1965

entries.sourceText: If our speech has no meaning, nothing has meaning.
entries.translationZh: 如果我们的言说没有意义，那么一切都没有意义。

entries.sourceText: There remains an amazing effort, daily, insistent.
entries.translationZh: 仍然存在一种惊人的努力，日复一日，持续不断。

entries.sourceText: Only by a continual effort can I create.
entries.translationZh: 只有通过持续不断的努力，我才能创造。

entries.sourceText: The effort of the hidden, without hope or bitterness.
entries.translationZh: 隐而不彰的努力，既不怀抱希望，也不心存苦涩。

entries.sourceText: At the end of the most terrible revolt, admit that you are nothing.
entries.translationZh: 在最可怕的反抗尽头，承认自己什么也不是。

entries.sourceText: No one can say that he has reached the limit of man.
entries.translationZh: 没有人能够断言自己已经抵达人的极限。

entries.sourceText: We are made to live in relation to others.
entries.translationZh: 我们生来就是要在与他人的关系中生活。

entries.sourceText: One serves mankind all together or not at all.
entries.translationZh: 要么服务于全体人类，要么根本谈不上服务。

entries.sourceText: The duties of friendship help to endure the pleasures of society.
entries.translationZh: 友谊的责任帮助我们承受社会生活的欢乐。

entries.sourceText: Death gives its shape to love as it does to life—transforming it into fate.
entries.translationZh: 死亡赋予爱以形状，也赋予生命以形状，并把它转化为命运。

entries.sourceText: It is the ability to admit that the adversary is right.
entries.translationZh: 那是一种承认对手也可能正确的能力。

entries.sourceText: Love is injustice, but justice is not enough.
entries.translationZh: 爱是不公正的，但公正并不足够。

entries.sourceText: For we are fighting for beauty too, aren't we?
entries.translationZh: 因为我们也在为美而斗争，不是吗？

entries.sourceText: Whoever greatly loves a value is thereby an enemy of freedom.
entries.translationZh: 凡是过度热爱某种价值的人，也因此成为自由的敌人。

entries.sourceText: The truth is that I could never believe in the Gestapo until I got kicked in the belly myself.
entries.translationZh: 事实是，直到我亲自挨了盖世太保的一脚，我才相信它的存在。

entries.sourceText: You begin by creating in solitude and think it's hard.
entries.translationZh: 你从孤独中的创造开始，并觉得这很艰难。

entries.sourceText: For most men, war is the end of solitude.
entries.translationZh: 对大多数人而言，战争是孤独的终结。

entries.sourceText: For me it is the definitive solitude.
entries.translationZh: 对我而言，它却是最终的孤独。

entries.sourceText: For the Greeks, beauty is a point of departure.
entries.translationZh: 对希腊人而言，美是一个出发点。
